newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura Sec shareholders sue former execs--Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Nomura Sec shareholders sue former execs--Jiji.

text.p: Shareholders of Nomura Securities Co Ltd have filed a representative shareholders' suit against four former executives, including former president Hideo Sakamaki, Jiji news agency reported on Friday.

The complaint said the former executives financially damaged Nomura, Japan's largest brokerage, by providing about 70 million yen of Nomura money to a corporate client linked to a "sokaiya" racketeer, Jiji said.
It said the suit was filed by a number of shareholders living in Tokyo.
Representative shareholder suits in Japan seek payment of compensation to the company as a whole rather than to the shareholders filing the suit.
A spokesman for Nomura said it would not comment on the report, saying the matter was between shareholders and the former executives.
In March, Sakamaki stepped down as Nomura's president to atone for the scandal. He remains an adviser to the company.
